gloss: To hit a stone with an egg; a futile effort.
teaser: Ever tried to fight a giant with a fragile egg? This idiom captures that struggle.
script: Welcome to Chengyu Bites — your quick summary on Chinese 成语. Ever tried to fight a giant with a fragile egg? This idiom captures that struggle. [break 1s] The phrase is: 以卵击石, yǐ luǎn jī shí. [break 1s] 以 (yǐ) - to use [break 0.5s] 卵 (luǎn) - egg [break 0.5s] 击 (jī) - to hit [break 0.5s] 石 (shí) - stone [break 0.5s] The idiom again: 以卵击石 literally means 'to use an egg to hit a stone.' Figuratively, it suggests a futile effort against a much stronger opponent. [break 1s] Here’s the story behind it: [break 1.5s] This idiom originates from ancient Chinese literature, illustrating the futility of challenging something far stronger than oneself. The image of an egg attempting to strike a stone is both vivid and poignant, reminding us of the importance of recognizing our limits. Those who ignore this wisdom often face dire consequences. [break 1.5s] Example one: 他以卵击石，根本不是对手。 [break 1s] He is hitting a stone with an egg; he is simply no match for the opponent. [break 1s] Example two: 面对强敌，他们的努力就像以卵击石。 [break 1s] Against a strong enemy, their efforts are like hitting a stone with an egg. [break 1s] Example three: 别以为你能以卵击石，还是想想其他办法吧。 [break 1s] Don’t think you can hit a stone with an egg; better consider other ways. [break 1s] So, to recap, 以卵击石 means to attempt the impossible or to take on a much stronger foe. Thank you for listening, and see you next time for another idiom. [break 1s]
